[id 240]
John has 54 candies.
John has twice as many as Robert $\Rightarrow$ Robert has $54 / 2 = 27$ candies.
James has 6 more than Robert $\Rightarrow$ James has $27 + 6 = 33$ candies.
Difference between John and James: $54 - 33 = 21$.

Dolly has 2 books. Pandora has 1 book. Total unique books = $2 + 1 = 3$.

[id 242]
Mike had 5 penpals, minus 2 = 3 penpals.
Each week, Mike sends 2 letters and receives 2 letters $\Rightarrow$ 4 letters total per penpal.
Total letters = $3 \times 4 = 12$ letters.
Each letter is 5 pages $\Rightarrow$ Total pages = $12 \times 5 = 60$ pages.
Time per page = 6 minutes $\Rightarrow$ Total time = $60 \times 6 = 360$ minutes.
$360 / 60 = 6$ hours.

[id 243]
Plan = 1000 minutes.
Calls to boss = $30 \text{ days} \times 15 \text{ min/day} = 450$ minutes.
Other calls = 300 minutes.
Total spent = $450 + 300 = 750$ minutes.
Remaining = $1000 - 750 = 250$ minutes.

[id 244]
Griffin starts with 24.
Kyle takes 5. Griffin is at 19.
Kyle gives twice what he took: $2 \times 5 = 10$ (to whom? Likely the group or a person not specified, but the key is Griffin's balance).
Wait, let's re-read: "Kyle took 5. Kyle gave twice as many as he took (10) [presumably to someone else/distributed]".
Ginger gives $x$ to Griffin.
Colby takes 3 less than Kyle took from Griffin: $5 - 3 = 2$.
Griffin's final total = $24 - 5 + x - 2 = 27$.
$17 + x = 27 \Rightarrow x = 10$.

[id 245]
Snails in A: 4. Snails in B: 32.
Difference in snails: $32 - 4 = 28$.
This difference is twice the number of fish in each aquarium ($F$): $28 = 2F \Rightarrow F = 14$.

[id 246]
Rate = $\$250$/hour.
Hours per day = 6. Days per week = 4. Weeks = 5.
Total hours = $6 \times 4 \times 5 = 120$ hours.
Total cost before discount = $120 \times 250 = 30,000$.
Discount = 10% of 30,000 = 3,000.
Final cost = $30,000 - 3,000 = 27,000$.
